clinician.trajectory_summary: A 22-year-old male presented with painless right facial swelling present since childhood, gradually enlarging over years to fist-size. Clinical examination revealed a fluctuant, compressible, soft, pulsatile swelling with bluish-red discoloration extending from the right eye's outer canthus to the mandibular border and from the mouth corner to the pre-tragus region, with intraoral involvement of the posterior buccal mucosa and soft palate. Key clinical features included a positive palpation test (elevated red-purplish lesion on compression) and slight temperature elevation. Initial workup with panoramic and submentovertex radiographs demonstrated multiple concentric calcifications (phleboliths) in the soft tissue shadow, pathognomonic for hemangioma. The diagnosis was established based on these typical clinical findings and conventional radiographic evidence. Following diagnosis confirmation and assurance of benign nature, the patient was referred to interventional radiology for definitive management.
